decks.name: Porchlight Rush / First Light
decks.summary: Win through early composure pressure with Quick runners, Steady attacks and Pierce finishers.
decks.explanation: Plan: Win through early composure pressure with Quick runners, Steady attacks and Pierce finishers. Opening hand: Keep a two-cost Neighbor and a Homestead. Lead with Apronfire Runner when a safe attack exists; do not spend removal on a harmless blocker. Districts and sequencing: Put an early attacker in each district; Council Spoon and Everybody Hums go with your largest ready group. This version adds two copies each of Moth-Tithe Keeper, Overdue Gardening, Neri, Borrower of Rain. Focus curve: 12 cards cost 0-2, 16 cost 3-4, and 2 cost 5 or more. Watch out: The plan can run out of cards or lose to Guards. Preserve a Spark for the defender window rather than spending all focus. Every card is explained in the library. These starter variations are playable presets, not tournament-balanced lists.

decks.name: Rain-Shelter Watch / First Light
decks.summary: Absorb attacks with Guards and district armor, then win with surviving Neighbors or an Undertaking.
decks.explanation: Plan: Absorb attacks with Guards and district armor, then win with surviving Neighbors or an Undertaking. Opening hand: Look for Teacup Custodian, a Homestead and a low-cost defensive Spark. Avoid hands full of expensive supports. Districts and sequencing: Use one protected district for your main army and leave a second Neighbor able to cover the other district. This version adds two copies each of Receipt for an Unarrival, Ink-Harvesting Engine, Pepper, Last to Leave. Focus curve: 12 cards cost 0-2, 16 cost 3-4, and 2 cost 5 or more. Watch out: Armor supports use the four shared support slots. Enemy support exile can dismantle your defenses; keep a replacement in hand. Every card is explained in the library. These starter variations are playable presets, not tournament-balanced lists.

decks.name: Common-Works Council / First Light
decks.summary: Reach eight accord by working on four Undertakings instead of relying on damage to the opponent.
decks.explanation: Plan: Reach eight accord by working on four Undertakings instead of relying on damage to the opponent. Opening hand: Keep an Undertaking, an efficient Neighbor and a Homestead. Establish a worker before committing several projects. Districts and sequencing: Place each project with a ready worker in its own district. Steady workers stay available to block, although they still work only once per turn. This version adds two copies each of Rebind the Common Atlas, Curtain Tangle, Brindle, Watchful Mechanic. Focus curve: 14 cards cost 0-2, 12 cost 3-4, and 4 cost 5 or more. Watch out: Projects occupy support space and enemy attacks can destroy them without an accord reward. Protect a nearly completed project. Every card is explained in the library. These starter variations are playable presets, not tournament-balanced lists.

decks.name: Supper After Dusk / First Light
decks.summary: Recover composure with Siphon, healing supports and careful trades, then outlast the opponent.
decks.explanation: Plan: Recover composure with Siphon, healing supports and careful trades, then outlast the opponent. Opening hand: Keep an affordable Neighbor and resource card; do not keep only healing when no board can defend you. Districts and sequencing: Put the Siphon keeper where it can deal real damage. Leave a Guard in the district receiving the most pressure. This version adds two copies each of Emergency Cushion, Orrin, Patient Calculator, Arrange the Lantern Supper. Focus curve: 16 cards cost 0-2, 10 cost 3-4, and 4 cost 5 or more. Watch out: Healing is capped at 24 and cannot save a lethal simultaneous combat batch after the game has ended. Empty-deck fatigue eventually overcomes healing. Every card is explained in the library. These starter variations are playable presets, not tournament-balanced lists.

decks.name: District Choir / First Light
decks.summary: Build a coordinated army around attack and armor auras, then convert multiple safe attacks into a lead.
decks.explanation: Plan: Build a coordinated army around attack and armor auras, then convert multiple safe attacks into a lead. Opening hand: Keep two affordable Neighbors and one resource. Play a body before an aura that currently helps nobody. Districts and sequencing: Auras only affect their district. Split some threats across the table while concentrating the relevant bonuses with your best attackers. This version adds two copies each of Overdue Gardening, Brindle, Watchful Mechanic, Unexpected Crumb. Focus curve: 12 cards cost 0-2, 14 cost 3-4, and 4 cost 5 or more. Watch out: Only four supports fit across both districts. Too many aura cards with too few Neighbors leave a weak opening. Every card is explained in the library. These starter variations are playable presets, not tournament-balanced lists.
